records.heading: b) Analytical Methods
records.text:
1H NMR, 13C NMR, and 19F NMR spectra were recorded on Bruker 400 MHz and 600 MHz
spectrometer spectrometer at 295 K in CDCl3 unless otherwise noted. Data for 1H NMR were
reported as follows: chemical shift (δ ppm), multiplicity, coupling constant (Hz), and
integration. Data for 13C NMR were reported as follows: chemical shift (δ ppm), multiplicity,
and coupling constant (Hz); Data for 19F NMR were reported as follows: chemical shift (δ
ppm), multiplicity, coupling constant (Hz). Chemical shifts were reported using the residual
solvent CHCl3 as the internal reference for 1H NMR (δ = 7.260 ppm) and CDCl3 peak as the
internal reference for 13C NMR (δ= 77.160 ppm). High-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS)
via electrospray ionization (ESI) was performed on a Waters XEVO G2 Q-TOF (Waters
Corporation). HPLC analysis were carried out on an Agilent system with Daicel columns.
Gas chromatographic (GC) analysis was acquired on a Shimadzu GC-2010 plus Series GC
system equipped with a flame-ionization detector.X-band CW electron paramagnetic
resonance (EPR) spectroscopy was performed using Bruker EMXplus spectrometer equipped
with standard resonator. Organic solutions were concentrated under reduced pressure on Buchi rotary evaporator. Column chromatographic purification of products was accomplished using forced-flow chromatography on Silica Gel (300-400 mesh).

subsections.heading: d) Chiral Ligand Synthesis
subsections.preamble:
The preparation of L12 was adapted according to previously published procedures.3 The
synthesis of L12 has been previously reported and spectral data are consistent.
Step I: L-(+)-Isoleucinol S1 (20 mmol, 2.34 g, 2.0 equiv.) and dimethyloxalate (10 mmol,
1.18 g, 1.0 equiv.) were dissolved in toluene (70 mL) and heated to 85 ℃. The reaction was
allowed to stir overnight and then cooled to room temperature with the diamide precipitating
out of solution as a white solid, then filtered and washed with petroleum ether to get the diol
S2 (2.73 g, 95% yield, white solid).
Step II: The diol S2 (10 mmol) was dissolved in toluene (50 mL) and heated to 90 °C where
upon thionyl chloride (1.72 mL, 2.4 equiv.) was added. The reaction was stirred for 8 h. After
the reaction is completed, it is cooled to room temperature, a large amount of petroleum ether
is added, and then the dichloro intermediate S3 is precipitated and filtered to afford (2.91 g.
90% yield, white solid).
Step III: To an oven dried flask was added S3 (6.0 mmol, 1.94 g) and phosphorus
pentachloride (14.4 mmol, 2.99 g, 2.4 equiv.) in 30 mL of toluene under Ar atmosphere. The
reaction was allowed to stir at 85 °C for 8 h before it was cooled to room temperature.
Toluene was evaporated under reduced pressure (80% yield, yellow liquid).
To an oven dried flask was added S4 (5 mmol), Et3N (50 mmol, 10.0 equiv.) and
3,5-di-tert-butylaniline (20 mmol, 4.1 g, 4.0 equiv.) in 25 mL of MeCN under Ar atmosphere.
Next, the reaction mixture was heated to reflux under Ar for 24 h. After been cooled to
ambient temperature, the volatiles were removed by rotary evaporation. the residue was
diluted with CH2Cl2 washed with saturated NH4Cl solution (100 mL×3) and water. The
organic layer was dried with Na2SO4, filtered and concentrated under reduced pressure. The
residue was purified by flash column chromatography (petroleum ether: EtOAc = 3:1) and
then recrystallized from hexane and EtOAc to give ligand L12.

records.heading: a) Synthesis of compounds 1a-1k
records.text:
Compounds 1a to 1e are commercially available.
A solution of NaH (11 mmol, 2.2 equiv.) and Me3SI (11 mmol, 2.2 equiv.) in DMSO (7
mL) and THF (6 mL) was stirred for 30 min at room temperature in a 50 mL flask under an
Ar atmosphere. Then a solution of aldehyde (5 mmol,1.0 equiv.) in THF was added dropwise
at 0 ˚C. After complete addition, the mixture was warmed to room temperature and allowed
to stir for 12 hours. The mixture was quenched with sat. NH4Cl and diluted with EtOAc.
Then the mixture was separated and the aqueous layer was back-extracted with EtOAc. The
organic layer was washed with brine and dried over Na2SO4. The solvent was removed under
reduced pressure and the residue was purified by column chromatography to give the desired
epoxides.1

records.heading: b) Synthesis of compound 1l
records.text:
A 100 mL round-bottom flask, flame-dried and equipped with a stir bar, was charged with
styrene (5 mmol, 1 equiv.) dissolved in DCM (30 mL). m-Chloroperbenzoic acid (10 mmol,
2.0 equiv.) was added, and the mixture was stirred at room temperature overnight. The
reaction was quenched with saturated aqueous NaHCO₃ and extracted three times with DCM.
The combined organic layers were washed successively with water, saturated aqueous
NaHCO₃, and brine, then dried over Na₂SO₄, filtered, and concentrated under reduced
pressure. The residue was purified by column chromatography to afford the desired
epoxides.1a

records.heading: c) Synthesis of compound 2-phenyl-1-tosylaziridine
records.text:
A round-bottom flask was flame-dried, and the alkene (1.0 equiv.), chloramine-T
trihydrate (1.1 equiv.), and MeCN (5 mL per mmol of alkene) were added.
Trimethylphenylammonium tribromide (0.1 equiv.) was then introduced, and the mixture was
stirred at room temperature under argon overnight. The resulting mixture was filtered through
a pad of Celite, and the filtrate was concentrated. The crude product was purified by column
chromatography.2

records.heading: General Procedure for the Synthesis of 3a on a 4 mmol Scale (1 mol%
records.text:
Catalyst Loading): In the air, a 100 mL Schlenk tube equipped with a magnetic stirrer
was charged with NiBr2(diglyme) (14.1 mg, 0.04 mmol, 1 mol%), L12 (30.5 mg, 0.048 mmol,
1.2 mol%), 4-biphenylboronic acid (6 mmol, 1.12 g, 1.50 equiv.) and sodium iodide (15
mol%). The Schlenk tube was evacuated and backfilled with argon three times, then EtOH
(16 mL, 0.4 M) was added, followed by the styrene oxide (4 mmol, 0.48 g, 1.0 equiv.). Then
the solution was stirred at 50 ℃ for 10 h. The resulting crude reaction was purified by
column chromatography using ethyl acetate and petroleum ether as eluent, and analyzed by
HPLC using a chiral stationary phase (0.46 g, 42% yield, 90 % e.e.).

sections.preamble:
General Procedure (GP): In the air, a 10 mL Schlenk tube equipped with a magnetic
stirrer was charged with NiBr2(diglyme) (5.6 mg, 0.016 mmol, 8 mol%), L12 (12.5 mg, 0.02
mmol, 10 mol%), arylboronic acid (0.30 mmol, 1.50 equiv.) and sodium iodide (4.5 mg, 0.03
mmol, 15 mol%) (Note a: If the epoxide was solid, it was also added at this step). The
Schlenk tube was evacuated and backfilled with argon three times, then EtOH (0.8 mL, 0.4
M) was added, followed by the epoxide (0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv.). Then the solution was stirred
at 50 ℃ for 10 h. The resulting crude reaction was purified by column chromatography using
ethyl acetate and petroleum ether as eluent, and analyzed by HPLC using a chiral stationary
phase.

sections.heading: VProcedure for the Synthesis of Racemic Products
sections.preamble:
Racemic products were needed for enantiomeric excess determination. Their synthesis
was carried out using the method we previously reported (Chem. Commun., 2020, 56,
109-112). In air, NiBr2(diglyme) (10 mol%), dtbpy (12 mol%), Arylboronic acid (1.5
equiv.) and sodium iodide (50 mol%) were added to a schlenk tube equipped with a stir
bar. The vessel was evacuated and filled with argon (three cycles). EtOH (0.8 mL) and
epoxide (0.3 mmol) were added in turn by syringe. The resulting reaction mixture was
stirred vigorously at 70 ℃ for 20 h. The mixture was purified by column
chromatography to afford the desired products.4
